phrases.text: The commentators differed. Most said the horses that gallop while they neigh, some said the camels, and some said the pilgrims who run from Arafat to Muzdalifa to Mina. Tabari takes the horses, because only horses pant.

phrases.translation: striking sparks of fire ˹with their hoofs˺
phrases.text: The commentators differed. Some said the horses strike fire with their hooves. Some said the horses kindle the war between their riders and their enemies. Some said it is the scheming of men, and some that it is the tongue. Tabari keeps them all, since God gave no sign that only one kind was meant.

Those who attack the enemy openly at daybreak, and some said the camels leaving Muzdalifa for Mina on the day of sacrifice. Tabari takes the general sense, that whoever raids at daybreak is covered by the oath.
They raised up dust in the valley. The word means the dust, and also the earth itself. The commentators say the horses made the earth fly with their hooves.

phrases.translation: and penetrating into the heart of enemy lines
phrases.text: With their horses they penetrated into the midst of the assembled army. The commentators say the assembly of the enemy, and some said it means Muzdalifa.

phrases.translation: Surely humankind is ungrateful to their Lord—
phrases.text: Man is ungrateful for the favours of his Lord. The word is compared to the soil that makes nothing sprout, and the tribe of Kinda is said to be named for breaking off from its father. The commentators explain it as the man who counts the misfortunes and forgets the favours.

phrases.translation: and they certainly attest to this—
phrases.text: God is a witness to that ingratitude.

phrases.translation: and they are truly extreme in their love of ˹worldly˺ gains
phrases.text: Man, because of his love of wealth, is exceedingly strong. The scholars differed over the sense: some said it means stingy, some that it means mighty. Ibn Zayd says the good here is the world, and the whole passage says: man is ungrateful to his Lord, and He is a witness over it.

phrases.translation: Do they not know that when the contents of the graves will be spilled out
phrases.text: Does this man, whose character is as described, not know, when what is in the graves is scattered and the dead are brought out and searched through.
phrases.ar: أَفَلَا يَعۡلَمُ إِذَا بُعۡثِرَ مَا فِي ٱلۡقُبُورِ

phrases.translation: and the secrets of the hearts will be laid bare—
phrases.text: It is distinguished and separated, so that what dwells in the breasts of mankind, of good and of evil, is brought forth.

phrases.translation: surely their Lord is All-Aware of them on that Day
phrases.text: Their Lord knows their deeds fully, what they hid in their breasts and what they did openly with their limbs. None of it is hidden from Him, and He will pay them back for all of it on that day.
